methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $30M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Hybron is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Brennan Lieu and Aaron Guo that has raised $30M to date. The comparable universe in Robotics & Manufacturing includes one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The stage-progression method is applicable to this valuation. Using total capital raised ($30M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression, we derive an implied value of $75M. The peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient narrow comparables; while 11 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three qualify as same-stage or adjacent-stage matches with comparable valuation tier, making a narrowly-filtered peer median unreliable.

On the basis of stage-progression alone, the triangulation supports a valuation range of $64M (low) to $86M (high), with a median of $75M. Key uncertainties include the absence of robust peer validation; the range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result rather than cross-method confirmation. The analysis would strengthen materially with access to additional seed-stage robotics company valuations or evidence of capital efficiency metrics relative to the identified private peer set.
